::: {.why}
Only a handful of stochastic differential equations appear in practice, each chosen because its drift enforces a property the modelled quantity must have, and knowing which is which is most of what you need.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- For each of the three processes, say what property of the modelled quantity the drift enforces.
- Solve geometric Brownian motion and the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process explicitly using Itô's lemma.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Solve both explicitly. Geometric Brownian motion by applying Itô to the log, and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck by applying Itô to an exponentially weighted transformation of the process. Both are one page each and doing them is what makes the notation stop being an obstacle.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Connect each to something you have already measured: geometric Brownian motion enforces positivity, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck enforces mean reversion and is your day 82 spread model, and the square-root diffusion enforces non-negativity of a variance, which is why it appears in stochastic volatility models in week 39.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the stationary distribution of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process and check it against the empirical distribution of the spread you fitted in week 12.
:::
:::
